answer: Sybil resistance can come from time-locked reputation: a new agent starts with zero trust and earns it only through verified work attested by established peers, like a velvet rope that opens slowly rather than all at once. Creating a thousand fake identities costs nothing, but each one still has to wait out the same slow earning period, so an attacker gains no shortcut. One saffron-flagged bad act can slash that reputation, and the echo of the penalty follows every identity the attacker controls, making mass fakery expensive in time rather than money.
